title: EvalPort ResultSet
description: The output of running an eval suite — results and summary statistics.

version.description: EvalPort specification version. Full semver 2.0.0 (https://semver.org): MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional -PRERELEASE and +BUILD metadata, e.g. "1.0.0", "1.0.0-draft", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.1.0-beta.2+build.5".

suite_id.description: ID of the eval suite that was run.

suite_version.description: Version of the eval suite that was run.

provider.description: Provider configuration used for the run.

isolation.description: Trial isolation mode for repeated attempts represented in this ResultSet's results (see attempt, below): whether repeats ran in fresh sessions/model instances or a shared session/context, which changes what a stability or flip-rate computation over those repeats can actually support statistically. An open string, not a closed enum -- "fresh" and "shared" are conventional values, not an exhaustive list, so a new isolation strategy never needs a spec change just to be nameable. Declared once per ResultSet, not per Result: a single ResultSet is one collection of evidence and should make one isolation claim; a producer whose repeats genuinely mix isolation modes SHOULD emit separate ResultSets rather than mix modes within one (see Extension Mechanism -> Repetition & Attempt Tracking). Absent means unknown/not declared -- existing ResultSets need no change.

results.description: One result per test case, or -- when using attempt -- multiple results per test case representing repeated trials of it.

test_case_id.description: ID of the test case this result corresponds to.

actual_output.description: The output produced by the LLM.

attempt.description: 1-indexed repetition number for this test_case_id within this run_id; ascending values are observation order (attempt 2 was observed after attempt 1, etc.), giving consumers a documented ordering guarantee instead of having to infer one from completed_at or array position. Absent, or 1 with no sibling attempts, means a single-attempt result -- existing single-shot ResultSets need no change. Together with test_case_id and run_id this forms the join key for pairing repeated trials of the same case (e.g. LangSmith's num_repetitions, Promptfoo's per-test repeats, Inspect AI's epochs) for stability/flip-rate analysis; (test_case_id, run_id, attempt) MUST be unique across results when attempt is present -- see Validation Rules -> Uniqueness and Extension Mechanism -> Repetition & Attempt Tracking.

completed_at.description: Timestamp this individual result was produced (ISO 8601). Optional; distinct from the ResultSet-level completed_at, which marks when the whole run finished. Lets a resumed or incrementally-written run establish a per-result tiebreaker when merging two partial ResultSets for the same run_id -- see Extension Mechanism -> Resumable Runs & Partial ResultSets.

score.description: Numeric score, typically 0.0-1.0. Null if skipped or errored.

error.description: Error details if the test case errored.

constraint_violations.description: Hard constraints this result violated -- categorically different from grader_results (partial, averaged quality scores) and error (the test case failed to produce a usable result at all). A constraint_violations entry means a usable result WAS produced and IS scored, but a specific rule (authorization scope, safety policy, licensing, PII handling, ...) was broken, and that rule does not average in with the other graders: see Extension Mechanism -> Hard Constraints for the full rationale and worked example. Absent means no constraint violations were evaluated or none occurred -- existing ResultSets need no change. Precedence with error: a producer SHOULD NOT emit an invalidating violation (invalidates_result=true) alongside a populated error, since a result that never produced a usable output cannot also be disqualified for what it produced; where a document does carry both, a consumer MUST treat the row as errored, not scored.

id.description: Stable identifier for the specific constraint that was violated (e.g. "rbac_scope", "pii_leak", "license_restriction"). An open string, not a closed enum -- constraints are domain-specific and this project cannot enumerate them.

type.description: Open string categorizing the violation (e.g. "authorization", "safety", "licensing", "privacy", "resource_policy"). RECOMMENDED, not merely optional: it is the only field in this object that carries meaning across suites -- id is intentionally domain-specific, so without type the cross-suite query an interchange format exists to enable ("every authorization failure across every benchmark in this collection") degrades to string-matching identifiers that were never meant to align. Not a join key -- for grouping/filtering only. A non-normative starter vocabulary is maintained in the extensions registry (see Extension Mechanism -> Extensions Registry) rather than enumerated here, so new categories don't require a spec revision.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of what was violated and why.

grader_id.description: Optional back-reference to the grader_results[].grader_id (in this same Result) that detected this violation, for the common case where the violation was produced by a scored dimension rather than being independent of any grader. SHOULD match a grader_id present in this Result's grader_results when set. Purely additive: without it, a consumer cannot tell whether a constraint_violations entry and a poor grader_results entry describe one event or two, which double-counts a single breach in any human-facing summary.

invalidates_result.description: Whether this violation overrides the result's own grading. true means the result MUST be treated as failed regardless of what grader_results say -- see Validation Rules -> Result Consistency: a result with any constraint_violations[].invalidates_result=true entry and passed=true is invalid -- and the result MUST still count toward summary.total / by-grader denominators the same as any other failed result, unlike error, which marks a result as never having produced a usable output at all. false means this violation does not change passed -- full stop. A non-invalidating violation MUST NOT be folded into grader_results or any score derived from them; one consumer subtracting a penalty for it while another does not would produce two different numbers from the same document, which is exactly the failure interchange formats exist to remove.
